step1_summary: Chief complaint: Fatigue with difficulty getting up in the morning and very low energy for ~2 months.

Symptoms: – Onset/Duration: began ≈2 months ago, coinciding with a new job. – Fatigue and low energy throughout the day. – Poor sleep / difficulty sleeping. – Decreased appetite (not eating much). – Difficulty concentrating, easily distracted. – Low mood (“mood is a bit lower”), anhedonia, decreased libido/sexual interest. – Shortness of breath on exertion during sports. No visual changes, no suicidal ideation.
Medications/allergies: Takes thyroxine (levothyroxine) chronically; no medication allergies.
Family history: Father died by suicide 15 yrs ago; otherwise non-contributory.
Social history: Married; started a new job 2 months ago. No other social/ETOH/smoking data provided.
Vital signs / exam findings: None recorded in transcript (tele-visit only).

V: Anemia (e.g., iron-deficiency or chronic disease) – can cause fatigue, dyspnea on exertion, poor concentration.
I: Chronic viral infection (e.g., EBV, HIV) – constitutional fatigue, low appetite, SOB possible.
N: Primary CNS neoplasm or pituitary mass – could cause low libido, fatigue; however no focal neuro or visual change makes it less likely.
D: Inadequately treated hypothyroidism – classic for fatigue, low mood, decreased appetite, dyspnea, low libido.
Nutritional deficiency (iron, B12, folate, vit-D) – poor diet & fatigue.
I2: Iatrogenic: Thyroxine under- or over-dose (non-adherence or wrong dose) causing hypo- or hyper-thyroid symptoms.
C: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia (late-onset) less relevant; no early life history.
A: Autoimmune primary adrenal insufficiency – fatigue, low mood, anorexia, SOB (deconditioning).
T: Post-viral fatigue / traumatic stress from new job change.
E: Major depressive disorder / adjustment disorder – core triad (low mood, anhedonia, low energy), sleep disturbance, appetite ↓, concentration ↓, libido ↓.
Obstructive sleep apnoea – non-restorative sleep, daytime fatigue, libido issues; SOB when exercising.

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Major depressive disorder (or adjustment disorder with depressed mood)
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Most symptoms map directly onto DSM-5 criteria (low mood, anhedonia, sleep disturbance, appetite ↓, fatigue, poor concentration, libido ↓). Onset temporally related to occupational stressor; family history of suicide increases vulnerability.
opposing_evidence: Primary goal expressed as wanting physical energy back rather than emotional; denies suicidality (though not exclusionary)
Reports not feeling distinctly ‘unhappy’ but ‘distracted’—could suggest another etiology

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Known history plus fatigue, low mood, reduced libido, dyspnea on exertion and decreased appetite are compatible with hypothyroid under-replacement. Dose requirement can change over time or with weight/job-stress; adherence unclear.
supporting_evidence: Documented history of hypothyroidism on thyroxine
Typical symptoms: fatigue, low energy, low mood, decreased libido, appetite changes, exertional SOB (muscle weakness)
opposing_evidence: No weight gain, cold intolerance, constipation reported
Duration started with new job rather than medication change, suggesting psychogenic trigger
If compliant, thyroid function may already be controlled

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Anemia produces fatigue, exertional dyspnea, poor concentration; decreased appetite could lead to iron or B12 deficiency.
supporting_evidence: Reduced oral intake over several weeks
opposing_evidence: No pallor, tachycardia, heavy menses, GI blood loss mentioned
Time course and mood symptoms could be better explained by depression
